members.working: Roasting ZnS with O2 at >850°C gives ZnO (white zinc oxide). Reaction of ZnO with HCl yields ZnCl2 (X). Treatment of ZnCl2 with excess NaOH precipitates Zn(OH)2 (Y), which on heating may form ZnO again. Thus <W> = ZnO, <X> = ZnCl2, <Y> = Zn(OH)2 (or ZnO). Zn in ZnO is Zn(II) (oxidation state +2), not +1 → (A) false. Zn2+ has d10 configuration (no d electrons) → (B) true (metal in W has d10). Geometry around Zn in Zn(OH)2 or ZnO is typically tetrahedral/distorted tetrahedral, not square planar → (C) false. Zn2+ is d10, not d9 → (D) false. Hence only option B is correct.

members.working: Reaction of carbon with sulfur at high temperature typically forms CS (carbonyl sulfide) or CS2? However, the most stable C–S product formed from solid carbon and sulfur at high temperature is CS (carbonyl sulfide) or possibly CS2 under certain conditions. CS has a bent shape due to the lone pair on sulfur, so option (A) could be considered correct. Reaction of hot coke (solid carbon) with steam (H2O) at 1000°C typically undergoes water-gas shift and produces CO and H2; the primary C-containing product is CO (carbon monoxide). CO has a bond order of 3 (triple bond), not 2.5, so option (B) is incorrect. CO is polar due to the C≡O bond dipole, so option (C) is incorrect. CO has no unpaired electrons (it is isoelectronic with N2, which has no unpaired electrons), so option (D) is correct. Therefore the correct option(s) are (D).
